answer: In node2vec, 3rd-order and 4th-order Markovian random walk transition tensors are not precomputed or stored in memory as explicit high-order tensors for million-node graphs. The method uses a biased random walk procedure (BRWP) that is 2nd-order Markovian (2OM): the next-step transition probability depends only on the current node and the previous node, not on a longer history. In practice, node2vec precomputes only pairwise transition probabilities for each directed edge (previous node, current node) over the current node’s neighbors, typically by building alias-sampling tables for those local distributions. This makes the memory cost proportional to the number of edges and local neighborhood sizes, rather than to the number of possible 3rd-order or 4th-order state tuples, which would be infeasible on million-node graphs. During sampling, the random walk generator (RWG) draws the next node from these cached local distributions on the fly. So the short answer is: node2vec does not store 3rd-order or 4th-order transition tensors in memory; it stores local 2nd-order transition tables instead.
